input.value: basement flooding with water damage to flooring, drywall, and stored items
hardwood flooring (buckled), drywall (soaked up to 1 foot), stored boxes (ruined)

input.question: What caused the basement flooding — a problem with your own plumbing/sump pump system, heavy rain or groundwater seepage, or another cause?

input.value: burst water supply line in policyholder's plumbing system

input.rationale: Damage to the policyholder's own home structure (flooring, drywall, contents) caused by failure of the policyholder's own plumbing system is textbook property damage coverage.

Extensive water damage to an entire basement including structural damage (buckled hardwood flooring, soaked drywall to 1 foot), plus ruined stored contents, likely exceeds $25,000 in repairs and replacement costs; requires prompt adjuster assessment and mitigation coordination.

input.claim_summary: Policyholder discovered extensive basement flooding caused by a burst water supply line in their own plumbing system upon returning from a work trip. Damage includes approximately 2 inches of water across the entire basement, buckled hardwood flooring, soaked drywall (up to 1 foot), and ruined stored boxes. This is a high-severity property damage claim requiring prompt on-site assessment, mitigation, and coordinated restoration work.
